initial_observation.encounter_context: presented with intermittent loin pain and a 3-year history of partial urinary retention
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: He had a 3-year history of partial urinary retention. History of fever, stone passage through urine, and hematuria was denied. His vital signs were within normal limits. Physical examinations were within normal limits. Laboratory examinations including hematology, renal function, and urinalysis found no abnormalities. Initial ultrasonography was performed and found pelvicalyceal dilatation and the proximal ureter was dilated, indicating pelvico ureteric junction obstruction (PUJO). Renal ultrasound was unable to identify the source of obstruction, thus further imaging was conducted.

evidence_items.source_text: Initial ultrasonography was performed and found pelvicalyceal dilatation and the proximal ureter was dilated, indicating pelvico ureteric junction obstruction (PUJO) (Fig. 1).

A renal computed tomography (CT) CT scan was performed and showed the normal size of the right kidney measuring 10.44 × 4.68 cm. The Parenchyma structure is homogeneous, pelvocalyceal system is widened. There was a hypodense lesion in the renal pelvis, extending to the proximal ureter that was not filled with contrast measuring 5.03 × 5.36 × 5.98 cm (Fig. 2).
The proximal right ureter was dilated. The cyst presses the right renal pelvic system and right proximal ureter causing PUJO, causing hydronephrosis grade III.

He was advised to undergo a nephrostomy for ureteral dilation followed by double J stent placement. A percutaneous approach for cyst removal was deemed very difficult in this patient, thus nephrostomy was conducted using an 8-8.9 Fr nephroscope. To be able to remove the cyst, the cyst wall had to be very thin and well-visualized to avoid renal parenchyma injury. However, in our case, the cyst wall was too thick and poorly visualized, thus cyst removal was not conducted. Cyst removal failed, thus we proceeded to perform ureteral dilatation. The double J stent was inserted and bleeding was checked. Four months after surgery, the cyst remained, but the patient was asymptomatic.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: In this case, we present a rare case of a PPC-causing hydronephrosis.
diagnostic_reasoning_verbatim_spans: The cyst presses the right renal pelvic system and right proximal ureter causing PUJO, causing hydronephrosis grade III.
In this case, we highlight the role of radiographic imaging in PPC.
In this case, the cyst was not filled with contrast, which differentiates it from hydronephrosis and renal cysts, both of which are usually filled with contrast.
